## Summary

There is a medium severity vulnerability in Traefik's TLS options conflict detection. The `Host` and `HostSNI` matchers treat a host name with a trailing dot (`example.com.`) and the same name without it as the same host, but the conflict detection does not. A router whose rule spells a host with a trailing dot can therefore serve a host that another router protects with client-certificate TLS options, without the conflict being detected and without the routers being put in error when `core.strictTLSOptions` is enabled. Anyone who can define a router, such as a tenant of a shared Traefik instance, can bypass the client-certificate authentication of a protected host. This is a gap in the fix of GHSA-j994-9gqj-9hwq, GHSA-g55h-rg46-x9c5 and GHSA-2272-4vv8-65ww.

Traefik v1 is not affected: TLS options were introduced in v2.0.0. The v3.0 to v3.6 lines are end of life and will not receive a patch; the remedy is upgrading to a patched v2.11, v3.7 or v3.8 release.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.64
